description: We are Orbital Farming, a team passionate about technology, agriculture, and sustainability. Together, we combine creativity and innovation to develop solutions that address agricultural challenges and promote responsible resource management. Different ideas, one mission: growing a more sustainable future through technology.
summary:
ROOT: From Dam to Root is a digital platform developed by Team Orbital Farming to support farmers in making better agricultural decisions through satellite data and environmental analysis.

The project integrates NASA satellite observations, climate information, soil characteristics, and agricultural models to evaluate water availability, monitor field conditions, estimate crop water requirements, and compare different planting scenarios. It also analyzes soil properties to identify suitable crops and assess their agricultural and environmental viability based on available resources.

ROOT addresses the challenges of water scarcity and changing environmental conditions by providing accessible information that helps farmers choose appropriate crops, optimize water use, and plan more sustainable agricultural activities.

This project is important because it promotes responsible resource management, helps reduce agricultural risks, and supports more informed decisions that can contribute to food security and sustainable farming.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

ROOT helps farmers and irrigation technicians in any dam-fed irrigation district answer one question before planting: how much water does this crop commit, for how many years, and how many hectares can the allocation cover? It shows each crop option as a multi-year water commitment, field by field, in the units the district uses. The dashboard is built around the map, works on a phone, and has five views:

  1. Overview: the pilot-area map colored by "Enough water?" or by crop, a water-budget slider with three reference allocations, a "less rain (−20 %)" switch, and the main indicator: the water already committed by perennial crops before a single hectare of annual crops is planted.
  2. My land and Crops and options: a close-up of each field (crop, yearly water demand, mapped soil, slope, area covered by the scenario) and its current rotation next to the alternatives, each with Water, Soil and Money rows and its reasons and benefits.
  3. Compare options: a step-by-step form (Your field, Your water, Your soil) where the farmer or technician enters what the satellite cannot see: the confirmed crop, area, available water, irrigation system, planting date and a soil test. ROOT shows the options side by side, each marked "Water coverage calculated" or "Needs a local check", with the reason, its source and how it is calculated. It gives no score and names no "best" crop. Consistency checks run in the browser, and the full calculation and evidence can be downloaded.
  4. History and rainfall range: a reference rainfall range per area, tested year by year against the years that came after (a time-based back-test with NASA POWER rain), and past events in the region. It does not forecast yields, the dam or daily irrigation.
  5. Field explorer: map layers (water term, crops, bare soil in the windy season, field memory over the years), terrain and runoff with a simulated storm, a 3D twin view, and a full field sheet with "Follow the drop" (dam, canal, field, crop, aquifer), a WhatsApp preview and a printable sheet for the farmer.

HOW IT WORKS

Every input is open and global. HLS v2 monthly greenness gives each field a year-by-year state and a rules-based crop map; fields the rules cannot classify stay gray instead of guessing. NASA POWER daily climate feeds FAO-56 to compute each crop's water need as a P10–P50–P90 band. Coverage = allocation ÷ need, and the map turns green, amber or red. NASADEM and GPM IMERG draw runoff routes and a reference storm. SMAP, MODIS, GRACE/GRACE-FO, GLDAS, GEDI and ECOSTRESS add regional context and field evidence. Field boundaries come from Fields of The World global predictions. One command rebuilds the site from validated data and runs every check; no figure is written by hand in the page, and the planner's rules are pure functions with their own tests.

PILOT: DR-005 DELICIAS, MEXICO

We built and tested ROOT where the problem is acute: two pilot areas of the DR-005 Delicias irrigation district (Chihuahua), 1,239 estimated fields. In 2025 the district received no dam water, and alfalfa and pecan, both perennial, covered 63 % of the area planted in 2016-17. The pilot shows the water committed by perennials, the 2025 year without dam water on the timeline, and featured fields: an alfalfa stand, an annual-crop field and a pecan orchard.

HOW IT SCALES

The method needs no local data to start: HLS, NASA POWER, NASADEM, GPM IMERG and Fields of The World cover the world. Each district constant (allocation marks, field efficiencies, water terms, rotation table) is kept, with its source and label, in one parameters file, and one command rebuilds the whole site. Local knowledge enters through the planner instead of being guessed. It has not yet been tried in another district: there, efficiencies, water terms and allocations must be checked, and the crop rules must be tuned to the local calendar.

BENEFITS

An annual crop can be skipped in a dry year; a perennial cannot. ROOT makes that commitment visible before the decision, in the farmer's own units, combines satellite data with what the farmer knows about the field, and keeps the decision with the farmer.

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

Review fields and options with farmers of the pilot areas, classify the remaining fields and assess the crop map's accuracy, and then set up a second irrigation district with its own parameters.

TOOLS

Python (data engine, validators, pytest), Google Earth Engine, NASA POWER API, AppEEARS, static HTML + JavaScript with MapLibre GL JS, d3 and d3-sankey, Atkinson Hyperlegible typeface, Playwright browser tests, GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages. It installs on a phone and works offline.

This tool supports, never replaces, the judgment of farmers and local experts.
